newsitem.title: GERMANY: German roasters shun cash coffee, sellers keen.
newsitem.headline: German roasters shun cash coffee, sellers keen.

text.p: Price fluctuations have prompted an exodus of German industry buyers from the physical market, where sellers are now keen to dispose of supply based on July futures, traders said on Tuesday.
"Central American origins and trade sellers are lowering differentials for May/June shipment but roasters are only operating at half speed and are covered for that," one said.
"The industry is preoccupied with retail price rises and their impact as we move into the summer season, when consumption is traditionally weak."
Market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard plans a third round of retail price increases this year in early June and its competitors have said they might follow suit.
New York futures on Monday saw May expire at 255.21 cents/lb, down 21.25 on the day, as profit-taking cut levels sharply after last week's 20-year highs.
July was off 6.90 at 246.25 and September off 6.35 at 220.00 cents.
Traders said sellers were concerned they might be unable to place spot material versus July and that they would need to roll over supplies into September, thereby incurring losses.
Against that, fundamentals were tight and the approach of the frost season in Brazil remained supportive, they added.
But futures were expected to ease amid producer meetings in London this week, which could bring an easing of export restrictions.
"Producers will have to come up with a scheme to appease consumers at these meetings," a trader said.
"It's hard to justify why September coffee should cost 220 cents when market intelligence shows 150-160 cents would already be a profitable level."
Roasters made sporadic enquiries for new crop coffee but sellers' ideas were too high, traders added.
Brazil arabica sellers were reportedly offering 50-55 cents/lb fob North Europe under New York July but Colombians were at 40 cents over.
The differential for Vietnam robustas was $220/tonne under London and Indonesians were at minus $150.
